failure_summary.description: Answers were too broad or too narrow despite existing instructions to return the requested modifier, full restored phrase, or shared name component.
The instruction to omit supplied category words can conflict with retaining words that are integral to a conventional proper name.
Candidates were chosen from prominent or related context instead of satisfying all identifying details in the clue.
A bare list of names can imply a request for their shared affiliation, but no rule explicitly guides that inference.

patch.reasoning: Most failures reflect noncompliance with existing answer-slot and evidence rules, so repeating those rules would not help. The edits address the distinct gap for bare name lists and resolve the conflict between omitting generic category labels and preserving canonical proper names.

edits.target: When the clue already supplies the category or type, return the distinguishing value alone: do not append a generic category noun, institution label, explanatory wording, or unnecessary title, subtitle, or suffix unless needed for disambiguation.
edits.content: When the clue already supplies a category or type, omit a merely descriptive category label, but retain words that are integral to the entity's conventional proper name (such as lexicalized place-name prefixes). Return the canonical name, not just a bare distinguishing element.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - When a prompt is only a list of names, use the context to identify a salient shared relation or affiliation and return that relation—not another listed name. Infer it only when the context supports a clear answer; otherwise do not guess.
